citations.claim: initial total energy before wall impact
outgoing speed after left-wall bounce exceeds incoming speed despite e=1

counterfactual.change: Changed bodies[0].e from 1 to 0 only; inelastic wall bounce removes energy gain so no violation in same 1 step.

explanation: Single body starts 0.1m from left boundary moving left at ~11.9 m/s, so it hits the wall within step 1 (6 substeps). With e=1 an elastic bounce should preserve speed, but outgoing speed is ~13.69 m/s, larger than incoming ~11.90 m/s, raising total energy from ~147.34 J to ~170.18 J with zero controller work. This indicates the boundary-wall impulse plus positional correction injects energy on impact (e.g. penetration correction added to velocity or restitution applied on already-separated position), exceeding the 10%+5J tolerance. Setting e=0 removes the gain.
vision_note: A single ball starts just off the left boundary wall and is in contact with it by step 1. It stays pinned at the wall with no visible bounce, so the energy gain is not visually obvious.
